regulatory_basis: Section 12, Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 r/w Rule 3, PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 - reported to FIU-IND
recommended_action: Freeze review by senior compliance officer; file STR within 7 days
narrative: Account CNRB243795 has been assessed as CRITICAL risk. Over the observation window it received Rs 1,853,934 and disbursed Rs 737,650. The account was surfaced by 3 independent detection layer(s) evidencing network chokepoint, fan-out / fan-in, pass-through conduit. The account does not act alone: it is one of 7 accounts in RING-01, alongside HDFC259211, HDFC801992, ICIC176070, ICIC511423, PUNB549145, UTIB119613, moving Rs 5,257,409 between themselves. Taken together the transaction pattern has no apparent lawful or economic purpose and is consistent with the placement and layering of proceeds of crime. A Suspicious Transaction Report is warranted under Section 12 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 read with Rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005.

grounds_of_suspicion.detail: Consolidation point: received Rs 1,853,934 from 3 accounts that were all funded by the single upstream source HDFC801992 one to five days earlier.

Received Rs 768,386 from ICIC176070 on day 11 and forwarded Rs 737,650 to UTIB119613 on day 12 - 96.0% passed on, 4.0% skimmed, held 1 day(s). The account stores no value; it is a conduit, which is the defining signature of a money mule. It is not a settlement rail: the behaviour occurs 1 time(s), not on a recurring schedule.

Chokepoint of the suspicious sub-network: betweenness 0.0061, +2.4 standard deviations above the other alerted accounts. A disproportionate share of criminal payment paths runs through this single account, so an account freeze here fragments the network rather than displacing it. Corroborates the primary flag; does not create it.

action_taken: Sub-network temporary hold recommended; account and its one-hop neighbourhood quarantined pending FIU-IND acknowledgement.
